title: Salma and the Unlit Lantern
logline: Salma tries to give light to Zuhdi and learns you can only share a flame you carry.
story: Zuhdi, who was emptying of the false self, lived in fear of the dark, and Salma, who carried deep perception, awareness of hidden truths, arrived with a grand offer of light. But Salma's own lantern was cold, kept only for show. However many times Salma pressed the dead lamp into Zuhdi's hands, no warmth would pass. Only when Salma stopped to kindle a true flame within did the smallest glow leap, at last, from one wick to the other. Salma learned that light is never given from an empty hand.
moral: You cannot give a light you have not first kindled within yourself.
